author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Keep controller order stable after reconnecting
summary: Test controller identity across sleep, reversed reconnect order, and app restart, then preserve stable per-device profiles or document a deterministic connection sequence.
heroAlt: PCSX2 SDL device configuration screen used to inspect controller identity and reconnect behavior

sourceLabels.pcsx2-controllers-current: PCSX2 mappings, profiles, ports, and peripherals
sourceLabels.android-controller-events: Android button, axis, and device event guidance

blocks.text: Test identity independently from discovery order
Determine whether Android changes the logical device identity or whether the emulator merely restores ports by discovery order.
Saving a lucky connection order does not prove that controller identity will survive sleep, battery loss, or app restart.

items: Both devices given unambiguous profile names that include model or adapter.
Current Port 1 and Port 2 assignments exported.
Battery levels sufficient for repeated sleep and wake cycles.
1. Launch with only the primary controller and record its Android and emulator labels.
2. Add the second controller and verify its isolated Port 2 response.
3. Close the app, disconnect both pads, and reconnect them in the normal sequence.
4. Repeat the launch and mark the assigned ports.
5. Disconnect both again and reconnect them in reverse order.
6. Compare device labels, event codes, and assigned profiles rather than controller color.
7. Put one wireless pad to sleep during a paused game and wake it.
8. Adopt stable device-specific profiles or document the only deterministic sequence supported.

blocks.text: Reversing the connection order distinguishes bindings tied to a stable device identity from bindings tied only to first-seen order.
The intended primary controller returns to Port 1 and the second controller returns to Port 2 across ordinary reconnect sequences.

items: Each physical pad is identifiable without relying on connection timing.
Sleep and wake do not silently duplicate a port binding.
The documented connection sequence gives the same result on two cold launches.
Both identical pads share one generic name: label the physical devices and preserve a connection-order procedure.
One device appears in a different Android mode: return it to the recorded mode before remapping.
A pad reconnects as keyboard input: inspect its mode switch or firmware behavior.
Only the game swaps players: verify its own controller-selection screen.

blocks.text: Restore the two exported profiles and reconnect devices in the documented known-good sequence.
Identical controllers may expose indistinguishable identities
If Android presents two units with the same logical descriptor and no stable identifier, a documented connection order can be more reliable than pretending the app can distinguish them.
